category_title: Struggling readers who use collaborative talk to clarify text confusion
student_description: Jennifer is a struggling reader who frequently disengages from independent reading due to cognitive overload from complex texts and unfamiliar vocabulary. She uniquely requires structured opportunities to verbally process information with peers, using collaborative talk and chunked reading to 'clean her head out' and readjust her schema.

criteria.rationale: Since Jennifer spends large amounts of time 'finding' a book to avoid reading, she needs explicit instruction on how to select engaging, appropriate texts.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes explicit lessons, routines, or guided practice for teaching Jennifer how to evaluate and select appropriate books.

criteria.rationale: Explicitly teaching connection-making strategies helps Jennifer build the schema necessary to adapt to new, complex information in texts.
criteria.check: The tutor incorporates ongoing, explicit instruction on making connections (text-to-self, text-to-text, text-to-world) to build her reading comprehension schema.

criteria.rationale: Jennifer relies on peers with diverse abilities to help explain confusing concepts and model comprehension.
criteria.check: The tutor plans for Jennifer to consistently participate in structured, heterogeneous literature discussion groups rather than working solely independently or in homogeneous groups.

criteria.rationale: Soliciting Jennifer's input on behavior and discussion rules fosters ownership and makes the collaborative process enjoyable.
criteria.check: The tutor includes opportunities for students to generate and agree upon their own behavior and discussion protocols for their reading groups.
